market_holds: Sealed baseline (2026-11-23 18:08 UTC): spot 134.78, front-expiry straddle 12.0%, event-implied move 11.05%, 25d skew +1.66 vol pts (mild downside premium), put/call OI 1.54, 'balanced' priced lean. Median absolute reaction over 8 prints is 5.28%, max 30.68% (the 2026-08-25 Q2 print: miss, FY EPS guide cut from $13.50-14.50 to $11-12, Foot Locker swung to a $40-80m FY operating loss). The stock fell on 5 of the last 8 prints. Run-in: -8.3% over 5 sessions and -6.7% over 20. From the 11-13 close of 149.70 to the 11-23 close of 133.90, DKS fell 10.6%, against SPY -4.1%, XRT -3.4%, Academy +3.3%, Nike -10.8% and JD Sports -6.7% (Yahoo daily bars). So about 6-7 points of the drop belong to DKS and its sector, on dated news: Nike's 11-17 8-K saying revenue declines through FY28 (Nike -6.3% that day), Williams Trading's 11-19 downgrade to Sell (PT $120; says Nike will cut Jordan allocations, Jordan is about 25% of Foot Locker US revenue, FY27 'about to get worse'), and JD Sports' 11-19 trading update (shares -4%). The rest is a tech-led market selloff. Consensus Q3 EPS is $1.38-1.42 on revenue of $5.06-5.08bn (Earnings Whispers 11-16, Fiscal.ai via Stocktwits 11-19). The Q2 call said Q3 is the toughest quarter for margins (gross-margin pressure 'most pronounced in Q3', about 50bp of SG&A deleverage). The DICK'S-banner comp guide is 2.5-4.0% and Foot Locker's is -2% to 0%. Sentiment is negative: the sell-side is split 13 Buy, 13 Hold, 2 Sell, with Wells Fargo on 11-13 expecting Q3 to beat the lowered bar.
view: This is the first print after a reset. In August management cut the year, told the market Q3 would be the worst quarter for margin, and said promotions would stay heavy through Q4. So Q3 EPS weakness itself is the consensus. The reaction will turn on three things: whether the FY guide holds, whether Foot Locker's comp shows the Q2 slide was the bottom, and what management says about Nike and Jordan supply into 2027. On the Foot Locker comp, the dated evidence leans better than the story the stock has traded on this past week. Q3 laps a -4.7% Foot Locker comp from Q3 2025. On a constant two-year stack from Q2 (-3.6% on -2.0%), that implies about -0.9% reported, which sits in the guided -2% to 0% band and is a visible improvement on Q2. JD Sports, the nearest public read on the US mall-sneaker channel, said on 11-19 that North America improved on Q2 over the same August-October quarter, partly because back-to-school demand shifted from July into August. That shift lands in DKS's Q3 too, since its Q2 ended in early August. Target reported November accelerating, and Stack said in September the sneaker problem was supply, not demand. Against that: JD's own core fascia in North America still ran -3.7% LFL with heightened promotions. Census sporting-goods store sales slowed from roughly +10.7% y/y in May-July to +9.1% in August-October, with October the weakest month at +7.1%. Combined seasonal hiring fell from about 14,000 to about 11,000, with Foot Locker down about 39%. And the call will be asked about Nike shrinking revenue through FY28 and cutting Jordan retro volume, a 2027 headwind management cannot price away. Net: a beat on a low Q3 bar with the FY guide held is a bit more likely than not, and the stock went into the print down 10% on news that is mostly about 2027 rather than this quarter. But the deciding line (the FY guide and the FY27 tone) is not visible, the last two prints fell, and the tape is swinging 3-5% a day. I lean modestly up and do not recommend.
unpriced: Possibly the sequential improvement in the Foot Locker comp. The easy Q3 2025 compare and JD's August-October improvement in North America point to a roughly flat Foot Locker comp. The week's selling (Williams' 'weak BTS traffic', Nike's FY28 outlook) traded the opposite story. I cannot show that consensus models a weaker Foot Locker comp, so this is a lean and not a proven gap.

recommendation.reason: Q3 margin weakness is the guided base case, and the dated evidence (easy Foot Locker compare, JD North America better in August-October, Target's November acceleration) tilts toward a held guide and a better Foot Locker comp. The recent drop is tied to Nike's FY28 outlook and an analyst downgrade, which are about 2027. But the deciding lines, the FY guide and management's 2027/Jordan tone, cannot be seen. The core DICK'S comp laps +5.7%, and the industry series slowed in October. The evidence does not reach 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A cut to the FY26 EPS range or the Foot Locker comp guide, or management quantifying a 2027 Jordan/Nike allocation cut on the call. Either would turn the reaction down despite a Q3 beat.

self_critique: The reaction is set by the FY guide and the 2027 tone, not by Q3 EPS. Management has every reason to be cautious on Foot Locker after Nike's FY28 warning, so a 'held' guide that narrows to the low end, or remarks about Jordan cuts, could sink the stock even on a beat. That is what happened after the last two prints. JD's core fascia at -3.7% is the closest like-for-like to Foot Locker and does not show a flat comp. The October slowdown in Census sporting-goods sales hits the hard +5.7% compare of the core business. And with SPY swinging 3-5% a day, the 13:00 window carries large market noise. These are enough to keep me from recommending, and I take p_up from 59 to 57 once.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped most: it showed the drop was tied to Nike and 2027 news rather than to Q3 data. The own-arithmetic two-year stack (P3) gave the one real lead. P7's 'line not visible' guidance kept me from overreaching. Searches kept returning prior-year results under a 'Q3 2026' label, which cost time and needs a date check every time.
